title.value: Learning with Rejection for Abstractive Text Summarization
title.justification: The title was extracted directly from the beginning of the paper where it is explicitly written.
title.quote:
Learning with Rejection for Abstractive Text Summarization

Meng Cao

Yue Dong

Jingyi He

Jackie Chi Kit Cheung

Mila / McGill University, Montréal, QC, Canada

extractions.description: This paper presents a novel training objective for abstractive text summarization using rejection learning. It aims to reduce non-factual content in generated summaries by allowing models to reject potentially noisy tokens during training. The method is demonstrated to improve the factuality of summaries compared to baseline models.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on improving abstractive text summarization through rejection learning, which doesn't directly relate to eco-responsible categories. It doesn't address climate-related issues or eco-responsibilities.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we propose a training objective for abstractive summarization based on rejection learning, in which the model learns whether or not to reject potentially noisy tokens.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no direct application or relation to eco-responsible sub-categories like renewable energy, pollution reduction, etc. The paper is centered on natural language processing techniques rather than environmental issues.
primary_sub_category.quote: The learning is based on the training dynamics of abstractive summarization systems where clean samples are learned quickly and noisy samples have relatively high loss.
